required_claim: Bridging 3+ scales simultaneously remains rare
Labeled multiscale datasets are expensive and scarce
MLIP/model transferability across composition and phase space
MLIP transferability across temperature and pressure
Model interpretability ("black box")
Generalizing universal MLIPs to surfaces and out-of-distribution systems
Generalizing universal MLIPs to interfaces and grain boundaries
OOD error is systematic bias, not noise, and traces to training sets biased toward near-equilibrium low-energy configurations
Multi-model ensembles underestimate uncertainty because uMLIP errors correlate with each other more than with DFT
Evaluation protocols are inadequate: single-point energy/force metrics miss workflow-level failures
Equivariant GNN-IPs carry l>0 geometric tensor features built from relative position vectors; switching off all l>0 interactions reduces the architecture to a conventional invariant GNN-IP
Within one architecture, the accuracy gain is a step change at the onset of equivariance (l=0 to l=1), with diminishing returns for higher l
Equivariance improves sample efficiency by changing the exponent of the learning-curve power law, not merely shifting the curve
Cross-method comparisons put the data-efficiency gap at up to three orders of magnitude in training structures
The learning-curve slope change is not attributable to equivariance alone: increasing message body order produces it with purely invariant messages
The strong form — that invariant architectures cannot represent directional information — is false; sufficient message body order recovers most of the gap
Data efficiency here means sample efficiency only; equivariance carries a compute cost that the founding evidence does not quantify
The claim that deep message passing prevents parallelization is architectural, not fundamental: an adapted spatial-decomposition algorithm retains high weak-scaling efficiency at five layers

The advantage is regime-dependent: at 10^6-10^7 training structures unconstrained architectures match equivariant ones on accuracy, with the residual cost appearing as training epochs rather than as an accuracy ceiling
Transferability to ionic transport is demonstrated at screening grade but not at quantitative grade, and the gap is measured rather than asserted
The magnitude of the target property is itself a generalization axis: accuracy degrades systematically toward high migration barriers
Reported accuracy can be decoupled from the underlying physics: good property predictions do not arise from good structural predictions, and good metrics do not require the physical input
Temperature is a demonstrated generalization failure axis for generative dynamics surrogates, with opposite-direction failure for structural and transport observables
Demonstrated generality is bounded by the ansatz, not by data volume: structural assumptions exclude whole classes of observable that no additional training removes

Where the reference standard is itself a foundational MLIP, its error on the target property is independently measurable — and experimental anchoring, where it exists, is the exception rather than the norm

One response to the transferability limit is architectural avoidance: designing the method so that the model is queried only on configurations close to its training distribution, rather than improving generalization
Permutation invariance is obtained in two places: order-independent aggregation over a neighbourhood, and a readout acting on the set of node states
Translation invariance is obtained by operating on relative interatomic position vectors rather than absolute coordinates
One rotational treatment builds scalar invariants from radial and angular basis functions and feeds only scalars to the model
The other rotational treatment carries geometric tensor features of order l >= 1 through the network, constraining every operation to be equivariant
Locality is imposed by a finite interaction cutoff together with decomposition of total energy into per-atom contributions over local environments
Total energy is constructed as a sum of per-atom contributions, and the training loss must contain a term depending on that sum
Symmetry can also be acquired non-architecturally, by training a generic non-equivariant model toward equivariance through a latent-space objective
Generalization to system sizes beyond the training distribution remains an open problem with the symmetry constraints already in place
The locality constraint fails where the physics is non-local, requiring explicit long-range electrostatic or dispersion terms, and its validity is condition-dependent
Relaxing strict locality through explicit long-range corrections improves transferability to out-of-distribution chemical space, not merely in-distribution accuracy
